lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Aeacus — for Pluto's sake — give me the tour. Show me everything in Hades.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Everything's a tall order, Menippus. But I can do you the highlights. That over there is Cerberus, as you know, and you've already met the ferryman who brought you across, and you saw the lake and Pyriphlegethon on your way in.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Right, I've got all that. And I know you do the gate. And I've seen the king and the Furies. Show me the people — the famous old ones in particular.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: That's Agamemnon. That's Achilles. Idomeneus, just there. That's Odysseus. Then Ajax, Diomedes, the pick of the Greeks.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: [chuckles] Well, well, Homer. So this is what the great set-pieces of your epics come to — flung on the ground, unrecognizable, shapeless. Dust, all of it, and a great deal of nonsense. [pause] Truly, as the man said, strengthless heads. — And this one, Aeacus, who's this?

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: That's Cyrus. That's Croesus. Above him, Sardanapalus. Above them, Midas. And that one over there is Xerxes.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: So you're the one Greece used to shudder at — yoking the Hellespont, planning to sail his fleet over the mountains. [pause] And look at the state of Croesus. — Aeacus, do me a favour. Let me give Sardanapalus one slap across the face.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Absolutely not. You'll crack his skull — it's a woman's skull.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Then at the very least let me spit on him. He's half a woman anyway.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Shall I show you the wise men too?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: By Zeus, yes.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: First up: Pythagoras.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Greetings, Euphorbus — or Apollo — or whatever you're going by today.

lines.speaker: Pythagoras
lines.text: And to you, Menippus.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Thigh's not golden anymore, I see.

lines.speaker: Pythagoras
lines.text: No, it isn't. [pause] Here, let me see — have you got anything to eat in that bag?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Beans, friend. So — nothing for you.

lines.speaker: Pythagoras
lines.text: Hand them over. The doctrines are different among the dead. I've learned that down here beans and the heads of one's parents are not, in fact, equivalent.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: This is Solon, son of Execestides. That's Thales. Next to them, Pittacus, and the rest. Seven in total, as you can see.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: The only cheerful ones in the place, Aeacus. The only ones not moping. [pause] And that one — the one covered in ash, like a loaf baked in the embers, all blistered — who's he?

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Empedocles, Menippus. Arrived half-cooked from Etna.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: My excellent bronze-sandalled friend — what possessed you to throw yourself into the crater?

lines.speaker: Empedocles
lines.text: A touch of melancholy, Menippus.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: By Zeus, no. Vanity. Pretension. A bad case of self-regard. That's what charred you up, sandals and all — and you deserved it. [pause] Though for all that, the trick didn't pay off, did it? You were found out. You were dead. — Aeacus, where's Socrates, then?

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Over with Nestor and Palamedes. Talking away, as usual.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Still, I'd like to see him, if he's around.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: See the bald one?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: They're all bald. That's not going to narrow it down.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: The snub-nosed one, I mean.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Same problem. They're all snub-nosed.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: Looking for me, Menippus?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Very much so, Socrates.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: How are things in Athens?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Lots of young men claiming to do philosophy. And if you just looked at the poses and the walks, you'd think they were the finest philosophers on earth.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: Yes, I've seen plenty of those.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Then you'll have seen the state Aristippus arrived in. And Plato himself, for that matter — one of them reeking of perfume, the other freshly trained in flattering Sicilian tyrants.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: And what do they think of me?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: On that score, Socrates, you're a lucky man. Everyone thinks you were an extraordinary fellow — that you knew everything. When in fact — and I suppose one ought to tell the truth — you knew nothing.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: [chuckles] I used to tell them that myself. They thought it was irony.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And who are these around you?

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: Charmides, Menippus. And Phaedrus. And the son of Cleinias.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Excellent, Socrates. Plying your old trade even down here. Not neglecting the beautiful ones.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: What else would I find more pleasant? Come, lie down beside us, if you like.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: By Zeus, no — I'm off to settle in next to Croesus and Sardanapalus. I expect I shall get a fair amount of laughter out of listening to them wail.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: And I'd better go too, before some corpse slips past me unnoticed. The rest of the tour another time, Menippus.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Off you go. This was plenty, Aeacus.
